submission.justification: Sensor-T1 has the best unirradiated single-hit resolution (6.0 um vs 9.0 um for T2 and 14.0 um for T3 at 150 um), but it is excluded by the radiation constraint: after 2e16 neq/cm^2 its hit efficiency is 82.0% with full depletion unreachable at maximum bias, far below the >=97% end-of-life requirement. T3 meets the efficiency requirement (99.2%) but has the worst resolution (14 um). Sensor-T2 reaches 98.5% efficiency after the same fluence and gives 9.0 um resolution, so it is the best-resolution option that satisfies the radiation requirement. Thickness 150 um is the only thickness at which resolution was simulated (2025 summary), so I chose it; the simulation summary offers no thickness scan, and resolution after irradiation was not measured in the documents. Both caveats are noted below as unknowns. The readout chip and bump bonding are compatible with all candidates, and power and cooling are not thickness-dependent in the documents.

requirements.requirement: Sensor must be one of the three candidate technologies
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T2 (planar, standard pitch) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Suitable for innermost-layer radiation environment (>=97% hit efficiency up to 2e16 neq/cm^2)
requirements.evidence: irradiation_testbeam_2026.md: T2 hit efficiency 98.5% after 2e16 neq/cm^2. (T1 at 82.0% fails; T3 at 99.2% also passes.)

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible single-hit spatial resolution in innermost layer
requirements.evidence: Among radiation-qualified options, T2 gives 9.0 um vs 14.0 um for T3 (simulation_summary_2025.md, 150 um, unirradiated). T1 is better (6.0 um) but is disqualified by radiation performance. Resolution after irradiation at 150 um was not documented, so the achieved value is unverified.

requirements.requirement: Readout chip compatibility (50x50 um pixels, 1.5 GHz/cm^2 rate)
requirements.evidence: readout_chip.md: all candidates are compatible; candidate_specs.md: all qualified for bump bonding.
No simulation or test-beam data on thickness dependence or on irradiated resolution for T2 are in the project documents; 150 um was chosen because it is the only simulated thickness.
